A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same GCR research, despite the changed title. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–D are readable and support comparison, including matching relocated and renumbered material.

before.justification: v1 reports original GeoGrid and DrawerWorld experiments, reward-shaping comparisons, learning curves, and GPT-4o/o3 autoformalization results.

after.justification: v2 reports original simulation results for GeoGrid and DrawerWorld, including learning curves and ablations, plus original autoformalization outcomes in Appendix C.

M1.justification: The learned labelling function, primitive value functions, compositional approximations, reward shaping, and RL procedure remain unchanged, as do the network architectures. Natural-language autoformalization was already included in v1 Appendix C.

E1.justification: Both evaluate four GeoGrid tasks and three tasks in the same Meta-World-derived DrawerWorld, plus GeoGrid autoformalization. Lift-Red-Box becomes Hold-Red-Box with the same task definition. Additional descriptions of demonstration behaviors do not establish changed dataset coverage.

E2.justification: The comparisons retain LTL-BC, Bespoke Reward Model, Bespoke BC, No RS, and High-Level RS. Appendix C still evaluates GPT-4o and o3. The qualitative MCQ-versus-Monte-Carlo comparison is retained and relocated.

E3.justification: Dataset sizes, the 10% validation split, retraining on full data, architectures, hyperparameters, training budgets, and 100/20 evaluation episodes remain unchanged. Autoformalization retains zero-shot prompting and manual exact-match evaluation; its prompt wording receives only a clarification.

E4.justification: The reward-shaping ablations, perceived-versus-actual reward analysis, and GPT-4o Logic error analysis remain. No new ablation, robustness condition, or empirical diagnostic question is introduced; Appendix A.1 adds conceptual interpretation.

E5.justification: Section 7.3 changes the repetition description from five independent RL runs to five repetitions of each method's training pipeline, clarifying the stated scope of repetition. Five-run averages, standard errors, and five autoformalization trials are retained; no increased run count is reported.

E6.justification: GCR's GeoGrid learning curves differ between v1 Figure 5 and v2 Figure 6, including a transient Safety decline near eight million frames. Tables 1–2 and the autoformalization results in v1 Table 4/v2 Table 8 retain their values and rankings.

T1.justification: v2 Appendix A.2 revises v1 A.1's option-return derivation by using the state-independent continuation approximation before taking expectations. This avoids the earlier unjustified factorization involving termination time and terminal-state value. The resulting approximation, definitions, and bound arguments remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract and conclusion focus the headline contribution on Reward Machine specifications and explicitly include qualified natural-language autoformalization, previously discussed outside those sections. The central claims of data-efficient grounding, compositional generalization, and effective reward shaping remain.

C2.justification: New Appendix A.1 explains the need for faithful proposition grounding and sufficient state coverage rather than trajectory coverage, and why expert demonstrations need not dominate the data. Appendix D removes discussion of adversarial proposition flips and malicious robotic applications.

D1.justification: v2 adds project code/video access information, reports code/data release in the checklist, and directs readers to released RM encodings. Appendix B.1 newly documents accidental and off-task demonstration behaviors. Existing architecture, hyperparameter, and compute disclosures are retained.

R1.justification: v2 adds citations concerning foundation models, symbolic planning, faulty rewards, and reward hacking, including Bommasani et al., Illanes et al., and Skalse et al. Hasanbeig et al. and Pavlick citations are removed, and the fuzzy-logic novelty discussion is revised. The overall positioning remains similar.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction, problem setting, and conclusion are extensively rewritten. v2 introduces an explicit contribution list, consolidates four research questions into three, gives natural-language interfacing its own subsection, expands Appendix A's organization, and adds the NeurIPS checklist.

P2.justification: v2 adds a framework overview diagram, redesigns both learning-curve figures with shared legends and revised axes and captions, reorganizes the PPO architecture table, and integrates previously end-placed appendix displays into relevant sections. These changes substantially revise the visual organization.

improvement.justification: The overview diagram and rewritten exposition improve accessibility, while Appendix A clarifies generalization assumptions and improves a derivation. Added access information strengthens reproducibility documentation. These are useful but limited gains: evaluation coverage and tabulated findings remain unchanged, and some specific misuse-risk discussion is removed.
